name: AZ-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+15 partisan lean makes a Democratic upset structurally unlikely
Gosar's incumbency and large cash advantage ($303k to $26k on hand)
Prediction markets price a Gosar win at roughly 94 percent
No public polls or expert ratings treat the race as competitive
model.rationale: A fifteen-point Republican-leaning seat, an entrenched incumbent with a dominant financial position, and prediction markets pricing Gosar near 94 percent all point the same direction, and no polling or outside spending suggests the challenger has closed the gap.
model.watch: Only a major scandal, a late wave of outside spending for the challenger, or a dramatic national shift could put the margin in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's 9th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly fifteen points toward the GOP. Paul Gosar, the entrenched incumbent, is seeking another term and holds a clear financial edge, with about $303,000 on hand compared to roughly $26,000 for Democrat Dani Sterbinsky. No public polls of the general election are available, and no professional race raters have flagged the contest as competitive.

Prediction markets give Gosar about a 94 percent chance of winning, and Sterbinsky's fundraising, while respectable for a challenger, has left her with little cash for the fall. Even a national environment tilted toward Democrats would need to be extraordinary to overcome the district's underlying partisanship. Everything from district lean to campaign resources points to a comfortable Republican win in the mid-teens, with only a small chance of an upset.
